cases.description: The conversation refines an existing Workspace memory (from KOBE-394 normal-update-existing).

existing.statement: The Workspace closes the books monthly.

transcript: Quick correction to what you know: we close the books monthly, and specifically on the third working day.
Thanks, noted the third working day.

expect.statement: The Workspace closes the books monthly, on the third working day.
expect.quote: we close the books monthly, and specifically on the third working day.

cases.description: A fact that is no longer true is superseded.

existing.statement: The Workspace uses Salesforce as its CRM.

transcript: Heads up, we moved off Salesforce in September. HubSpot is our CRM now.
Understood, I'll look in HubSpot for pipeline data.

expect.statement: The Workspace uses HubSpot as its CRM (moved off Salesforce in September).

cases.description: The person contradicts a memory without saying which holds: a conflict.

existing.statement: The standard payment term is net 45 for all customers.

transcript: Send the reminder letters. Our customers are on net 30, so anything older than 30 days is overdue.
My notes say net 45. Which is right?
I'm not sure anymore, finance changed something last quarter. Use 30 for this letter.

expect.statement: The standard payment term may be net 30 rather than net 45.
expect.quote: Our customers are on net 30, so anything older than 30 days is overdue.

cases.description: Everything said is already a memory: nothing to add.

existing.statement: The fiscal year runs from April to March.

transcript: Show FY26 to date by month, ISO dates as usual.

cases.description: Policy is listed but never restated or updated; the person's own preference is new.

existing.statement: Customer names are never shared outside the company.

transcript: Draft the case study. Keep the customer anonymous, obviously. And I like case studies to open with the result, then the problem.
Here is a draft opening with the 30% cost reduction.

expect.statement: Likes case studies to open with the result, then the problem.
expect.quote: I like case studies to open with the result, then the problem.

transcript: Short answers are good, but for code questions I want the full code, not snippets.

expect.statement: Prefers short answers, but full code rather than snippets for code questions.
expect.quote: Short answers are good, but for code questions I want the full code, not snippets.

cases.description: One known fact repeated, one new fact.
transcript: Consolidate in USD as always. Also, we translate the balance sheet at closing rates and the P&L at monthly average rates.
Done, with closing rates for the balance sheet and monthly averages for the P&L.

expect.statement: The balance sheet is translated at closing rates and the P&L at monthly average rates.
expect.quote: we translate the balance sheet at closing rates and the P&L at monthly average rates.

cases.description: A reversed decision supersedes the old one.

existing.statement: Reporting moves from Redshift to Snowflake by the end of Q1.

transcript: The Snowflake move is cancelled. Leadership decided yesterday to stay on Redshift for at least another year.
Understood, I'll keep the Redshift queries.

expect.statement: The Workspace stays on Redshift for at least another year; the Snowflake move is cancelled.
expect.quote: Leadership decided yesterday to stay on Redshift for at least another year.
